stages.label: Target & druggability
stages.blurb: Is the target real, and is there a pocket worth attacking?

stages.label: Protein structures
stages.blurb: Get and prepare the receptor you will design against.

stages.label: Binding sites & pockets
stages.blurb: Find, characterise and score the site itself.

stages.label: Docking & virtual screening
stages.blurb: Pose prediction, rescoring, screening at scale.

stages.label: Dynamics & free energy
stages.blurb: Simulation, enhanced sampling, binding free energies.

stages.label: Quantum chemistry
stages.blurb: DFT, semiempirical methods, reaction profiles, parameters.

stages.label: QSAR & property models
stages.blurb: Predicting activity and properties, and the ML under it.

stages.label: Synthesis & retrosynthesis
stages.blurb: Can it be made, by what route, from what building blocks.

stages.label: Peptides & protein design
stages.blurb: Macrocycles, peptides, biologics and protein engineering.

stages.label: Clinical & competitive
stages.blurb: Trials, labels, approvals, real-world safety signals.

stages.label: Benchmarks & datasets
stages.blurb: Reference sets that tell you whether a method works.

stages.label: Visualisation
stages.blurb: Looking at poses, structures and molecules.

tools.name: GPCRdb
tools.description: Structures, mutations, ligands and conformational states across the GPCR superfamily, on a shared residue numbering.

tools.name: canSAR
tools.description: Target assessment built for drug discovery rather than biology: structural druggability, existing chemistry, clinical precedent and safety signals for one protein on one page.

tools.name: DrugCentral
tools.description: Approved drugs with their targets, measured activities, indications and pharmacology — the fastest way to see what already works on a target family.

tools.name: FTMap
tools.description: Computational solvent mapping: docks small organic probes across the surface to find consensus hot spots — where a ligand could get real binding energy, before any chemistry starts.

tools.name: KLIFS
tools.description: Kinase-ligand structures on a common 85-residue binding-site numbering, so binding modes and DFG/αC states are comparable across the whole kinome.

tools.name: Open Targets Platform
tools.description: Target-disease association evidence aggregated from genetics, omics, literature and known drugs; the standard first stop for target triage.

tools.name: SwissTargetPrediction
tools.description: Predicts a small molecule's likely protein targets by combining 2D and 3D similarity to compounds with measured activity. The web standard for a first pass, with the caveat that it can only propose targets that already have ligands.

tools.name: Therapeutic Target Database
tools.description: Targets classified by clinical stage with the drugs against each, useful for judging how contested a target already is.

tools.name: BATMAN-TCM
tools.description: Predicts targets for the constituents of a herbal formula and runs the enrichment over them, built specifically for the multi-compound multi-target case.

tools.name: BioGRID
tools.description: Curated protein, genetic and chemical interactions from primary literature.

tools.name: cBioPortal
tools.description: Interactive exploration of large-scale cancer genomics studies (mutation, CNA, expression, survival).

tools.name: ChEMBL multitask target prediction
tools.description: ChEMBL's own multitask neural network for target prediction, shipped as a model you run locally instead of a web form. Trained on ChEMBL activities, with runnable examples in Python, C++, Julia and JavaScript.

tools.name: clusterProfiler
tools.description: The R package most enrichment figures in the literature come from: over-representation and GSEA across GO, KEGG and custom sets, with the plots built in.

tools.name: CTD
tools.description: Comparative Toxicogenomics Database: curated chemical-gene, chemical-disease and gene-disease relationships from the literature. The evidence layer under most chemical-centric network studies.

tools.name: DepMap
tools.description: Genome-wide CRISPR and RNAi essentiality across ~1,100 cancer cell lines, plus expression, mutation and drug-sensitivity data.

tools.name: DisGeNET
tools.description: Gene-disease and variant-disease association collection used for target-indication rationale.

tools.name: Enrichr
tools.description: Fast web enrichment against 200+ gene set libraries, with an API.

tools.name: Ensembl
tools.description: Genome annotation, variation, comparative genomics and the BioMart/REST query layer over them.

tools.name: g:Profiler
tools.description: Functional enrichment, ortholog mapping and ID conversion with a stable versioned API.

tools.name: GeneCards
tools.description: Aggregated gene-centric annotation across ~150 sources; free for academic browsing.

tools.name: GeneMANIA
tools.description: Predicts function by placing a gene in a composite network of co-expression, physical interaction and pathway membership, and names the evidence for each edge.

tools.name: gnomAD
tools.description: Population variation with loss-of-function constraint: whether humans tolerate losing this gene is the cheapest safety signal you will get on a target.

tools.name: GSEA / MSigDB
tools.description: Gene set enrichment analysis and the curated hallmark/canonical gene set collections behind it.

tools.name: GTEx Portal
tools.description: Bulk and single-nucleus expression and eQTL data across 50+ human tissues.

tools.name: GWAS Catalog
tools.description: Curated genotype-phenotype associations — the genetic evidence line that most strongly predicts clinical success.

tools.name: Human Protein Atlas
tools.description: Tissue, single-cell, subcellular and pathology protein expression maps; used to check target expression and off-tissue risk.

tools.name: KEGG
tools.description: Pathway, disease and drug maps; free for academic web use, licensed for bulk download.

tools.name: Metascape
tools.description: Gene list annotation and enrichment across many ontologies at once, with a protein-protein interaction module. The fastest way from a hit list to a defensible pathway story.

tools.name: NetworkAnalyst
tools.description: Network and enrichment analysis in the browser, from a gene or protein list to a protein-protein interaction subnetwork with statistics attached.

tools.name: OmniPath
tools.description: Unified signalling network: pathways, enzyme-substrate, complexes and annotations from 100+ resources, with a Python client.

tools.name: PDBe-KB
tools.description: Aggregates every structural annotation for a protein — ligand sites, interfaces, conformational states — across all its PDB entries at once.

tools.name: Pharos / TCRD
tools.description: NIH IDG portal ranking the druggable genome by how well each target is studied (Tclin/Tchem/Tbio/Tdark).

tools.name: PPB2
tools.description: Polypharmacology Browser 2: nearest-neighbour search over ChEMBL by ECfp4, Xfp shape-pharmacophore or MQN fingerprints, optionally combined with a naive Bayes model fitted on the fly. Useful because you can compare what different descriptors nominate.

tools.name: Probe Miner
tools.description: Scores public chemical probes on potency, selectivity and cell activity, so you can tell whether the compound in a paper actually supports its conclusion.

tools.name: Reactome
tools.description: Peer-reviewed pathway database with pathway enrichment and network analysis tools.

tools.name: SEA
tools.description: Similarity Ensemble Approach: relates targets by the chemistry of their ligands, so a compound's likely off-targets fall out of its structure. Long-standing polypharmacology check.

tools.name: STITCH
tools.description: Known and predicted chemical-protein interactions across species, useful for a first pass at what else a chemotype might touch.

tools.name: STRING
tools.description: Protein-protein association networks combining experiments, co-expression, text mining and orthology transfer.

tools.name: TargetNet
tools.description: Runs a per-target QSAR model across 623 human proteins and returns a predicted activity profile rather than a ranked shortlist. Each target carries its own model, so applicability varies target by target.

tools.name: UniProt
tools.description: Reference protein sequence and functional annotation; the identifier backbone every other resource maps to.

tools.name: MODELLER
tools.description: Comparative/homology modelling by satisfaction of spatial restraints; free academic licence.

tools.name: SWISS-MODEL
tools.description: Automated homology modelling server with quality estimation (QMEANDisCo) and oligomeric state prediction.

tools.name: AlphaFill
tools.description: Transplants ligands, cofactors and metal ions into AlphaFold models by sequence and structure similarity. AlphaFold predicts the fold, not the metal, so a metalloprotein model without this step has an empty site.

tools.name: AlphaFold 3
tools.description: Joint structure prediction for proteins, nucleic acids, ligands and ions; weights are available for non-commercial use on request.

tools.name: AlphaFold Protein Structure DB
tools.description: Predicted structures for 200M+ proteins with per-residue pLDDT confidence.

tools.name: Biopython
tools.description: General bioinformatics library: sequence and structure parsing, alignment, PDB handling.

tools.name: Chai-1
tools.description: Open multimodal biomolecular complex prediction model, free for commercial use.

tools.name: CheckMyMetal
tools.description: Validates metal sites in deposited or refined structures against expected coordination number, geometry and donor distances. Mis-assigned metals are common; check before you build a docking model on one.

tools.name: ColabFold
tools.description: AlphaFold2 and friends with MMseqs2 doing the MSA, which turns an overnight job into minutes; the usual way people actually run structure prediction.

tools.name: DSSP
tools.description: Reference secondary-structure and solvent-accessibility assignment from 3D coordinates.

tools.name: Foldseek
tools.description: Structure search at sequence-search speed; finds structural homologues across the whole PDB and AlphaFold DB in seconds.

tools.name: Fragalysis
tools.description: Diamond's browser for fragment screening campaigns: every hit, its density and its pose, in one place, with the merged designs that came from them.

tools.name: HH-suite3
tools.description: HMM-HMM remote homology detection for hard templates and deep MSAs.

tools.name: MMseqs2
tools.description: Ultra-fast sequence search and clustering; the MSA engine behind ColabFold.

tools.name: PanDDA
tools.description: Finds fragment binding events that conventional refinement misses, by comparing many datasets to a ground state — the analysis that makes crystallographic fragment screening work at all.

tools.name: PDB2PQR / APBS
tools.description: Assigns titration states and charges/radii, then solves Poisson-Boltzmann electrostatics.

tools.name: PDBFixer
tools.description: Repairs PDB files for simulation: missing residues and heavy atoms, non-standard residues, protonation, solvation.

tools.name: PROPKA
tools.description: Empirical pKa prediction for protein residues and ligands, used to set protonation before docking or MD.

tools.name: RCSB PDB
tools.description: The experimental structure archive plus search, validation and ligand chemistry services.

tools.name: P2Rank
tools.description: Machine-learning ligand-binding site prediction from structure; fast, template-free, used inside several docking pipelines.

tools.name: CASTp
tools.description: Computed atlas of surface topography: analytic pocket and cavity measurement.

tools.name: InterMetalDB
tools.description: Intermolecular metal sites, where the ion bridges two chains or a chain and a ligand; the place to look before assuming a metal-mediated contact is an artefact.

tools.name: LMetalSite
tools.description: Alignment-free metal-binding residue prediction from sequence alone, via a protein language model; the fallback when there is no structure at all.

tools.name: MIB2
tools.description: Predicts metal ion-binding residues and models the ion into the structure, by fragment transfer from known sites; covers a dozen biologically common ions.

tools.name: PrankWeb
tools.description: Web front end for P2Rank with conservation scoring and in-browser visualisation.

tools.name: ZincBind
tools.description: Curated database of zinc binding sites extracted from the PDB, grouped by coordinating residue family and site type.

tools.name: BioBrigit
tools.description: Predicts how a metal ion travels through a protein to reach its site, not just where the site is. Combines a 3D CNN over the biochemical environment with known bioinorganic coordination preferences.

tools.name: BioMetAll
tools.description: Geometry-based search for candidate metal-binding sites using only backbone and side-chain positions, so it finds sites in apo and predicted structures. This is the published v1; v2 adds scoring and metal discrimination.

tools.name: BioMetAll v2
tools.description: The current BioMetAll: adds a score per candidate site, discriminates between metals rather than reporting any site, and uses side-chain descriptors instead of backbone geometry alone.

tools.name: fpocket
tools.description: Voronoi-based pocket detection and druggability scoring, with mdpocket for pocket dynamics over MD trajectories.

tools.name: Fragment Hotspot Maps
tools.description: CCDC's hotspot maps score a pocket by the interaction patterns seen in crystal structures, showing which subpockets are worth growing into.

tools.name: mdpocket
tools.description: The fpocket companion that tracks pocket volume and persistence across an MD trajectory — how you find a cryptic pocket that only opens some of the time.

tools.name: MESPEUS
tools.description: Metal coordination geometry measured across the PDB: bond lengths, angles and donor-set frequencies per metal. The reference for judging whether a site's geometry is physically reasonable.

tools.name: Metal3D
tools.description: 3D CNN predicting zinc site location and probability density directly from protein geometry; useful when the apo structure has no ion modelled.

tools.name: MetalPDB
tools.description: Every metal site in the PDB, abstracted into minimal functional sites so you can compare coordination geometry and donor sets across unrelated folds.

tools.name: PocketMiner
tools.description: Predicts where cryptic pockets are likely to open from a single structure, so you know whether long sampling is worth running at all.

tools.name: ProteinsPlus / DoGSiteScorer
tools.description: Pocket detection with druggability scores, plus protonation (Protoss) and pose analysis tools.

tools.name: gnina
tools.description: Fork of smina with convolutional neural network scoring and rescoring, run alongside the empirical score rather than instead of it.

tools.name: ProLIF
tools.description: Protein-ligand interaction fingerprints from structures or trajectories, so poses can be compared on interactions rather than score.

tools.name: DockStream
tools.description: AstraZeneca's docking wrapper exposing several backends to generative loops such as REINVENT. Archived and unmaintained since 2023: usable as a reference, but plan to pin its dependencies.

tools.name: EasyDock
tools.description: Python wrapper unifying Vina/smina/gnina runs with SQLite bookkeeping and protonation handling.

tools.name: AutoDock Vina
tools.description: The most widely used open docking engine; fast, well-validated, and the baseline every other method is measured against.

tools.name: HADDOCK3
tools.description: Integrative docking driven by experimental restraints, and the practical open route to protein-protein and ternary complexes such as PROTAC-induced interfaces.

tools.name: LigPlot+
tools.description: 2D schematic diagrams of protein-ligand interactions for figures and pose triage.

tools.name: MetalDock
tools.description: Docks organometallic and metal-complex ligands into proteins, DNA and other biomolecules, optimising the complex with QM and generating the metal parameters the docking needs.

tools.name: SwissDock
tools.description: Free docking web service (AutoDock Vina and Attracting Cavities backends) for occasional runs.

tools.name: Uni-Dock
tools.description: GPU-accelerated docking engine reaching thousands of molecules per second per GPU.

tools.name: Vina-GPU 2.1
tools.description: GPU-parallel Vina, and the QuickVina2-GPU variant alongside it, giving one to two orders of magnitude speedup on large screens.

tools.name: ODDT
tools.description: Open Drug Discovery Toolkit: rescoring functions (RFScore, NNScore), interaction fingerprints and VS metrics.

tools.name: Meeko
tools.description: Prepares ligands and receptors for AutoDock: PDBQT writing, macrocycle handling, covalent setups.

tools.name: rDock
tools.description: Fast open-source docking for proteins and nucleic acids, with pharmacophore and tethered-scaffold restraints.

tools.name: GaudiMM
tools.description: Multi-objective genetic algorithm that optimises binding, geometry and any other objective you define at once, instead of collapsing them into one score. Handles metal coordination and flexible systems that fixed-receptor docking cannot express.

tools.name: AutoDock4Zn
tools.description: Zinc force field for AutoDock4 adding directional pseudo-atoms around the ion, so tetrahedral coordination is rewarded geometrically rather than as undirected electrostatics.

tools.name: DOCK 6
tools.description: UCSF's long-standing anchor-and-grow docking program with a wide scoring-function suite.

tools.name: Glide (Schrödinger)
tools.description: Industry-standard commercial docking (HTVS/SP/XP) with the Maestro preparation stack.

tools.name: GOLD (CCDC)
tools.description: Genetic-algorithm docking with CSD-derived knowledge and well-validated scoring functions.

tools.name: KarmaDock
tools.description: Deep-learning docking that scores and optimises poses in one pass, fast enough to make a neural method viable for library-scale screening.

tools.name: MOE (CCG)
tools.description: Integrated commercial modelling environment: docking, pharmacophores, biologics and QSAR in one platform.

tools.name: NeuralPLexer
tools.description: Predicts protein-ligand complex structures directly, generating the receptor conformation alongside the pose instead of docking into a fixed one.

tools.name: Pharmit
tools.description: Interactive pharmacophore and shape search over billions of purchasable compounds, with in-browser minimisation.

tools.name: PLIP
tools.description: Detects and reports non-covalent protein-ligand interactions from a complex; standard for pose interpretation.

tools.name: Ringtail
tools.description: Stores and filters millions of docking results in SQLite so large screens stay queryable.

tools.name: smina
tools.description: Vina fork with flexible scoring-function specification and much easier custom-term development.

tools.name: SurfDock
tools.description: Surface-informed diffusion docking: conditions pose generation on the molecular surface of the pocket rather than atoms alone.

tools.name: VirtualFlow
tools.description: Open workflow for distributing ultra-large virtual screens (billions of ligands) across HPC and cloud.

tools.name: MDAnalysis
tools.description: Python library for reading and analysing trajectories from essentially every MD format.

tools.name: MDTraj
tools.description: Fast trajectory IO and geometric analysis with a lightweight NumPy-native API.

tools.name: PLUMED
tools.description: Plugin for enhanced sampling and free-energy methods (metadynamics, umbrella sampling) across MD engines.

tools.name: GROMACS
tools.description: The most widely used open MD engine; fast on CPU and GPU, with a complete analysis toolchain.

tools.name: ACPYPE
tools.description: Converts Antechamber/GAFF ligand parameters into GROMACS, CHARMM and other topologies.

tools.name: gmx_MMPBSA
tools.description: MM-PBSA/MM-GBSA end-state binding free energies from GROMACS trajectories, with per-residue decomposition.

tools.name: Martini
tools.description: Coarse-grained force field for large-scale membrane, protein and lipid-nanoparticle simulation.

tools.name: TorchANI
tools.description: PyTorch implementation of the ANI neural network potentials for organic molecules.

tools.name: OpenMM
tools.description: GPU-accelerated MD as a Python library rather than a monolithic binary — the easiest engine to script custom simulation protocols around.

tools.name: OpenFF Toolkit
tools.description: Open Force Field small-molecule parameterisation with direct OpenMM/GROMACS export.

tools.name: OpenFE
tools.description: Open Free Energy: production relative and absolute binding free-energy campaigns with reproducible protocols.

tools.name: openmmtools
tools.description: Replica exchange, alchemical factories and well-tested integrators for OpenMM — the standard way to run REST2/parallel tempering in Python.

tools.name: alchemlyb
tools.description: Standard estimators (MBAR, BAR, TI) and convergence diagnostics for alchemical free-energy data.

tools.name: WESTPA
tools.description: Weighted ensemble sampling: runs many short trajectories with statistical reweighting to reach rare events and extract rate constants, rather than waiting for one long trajectory to cross the barrier.

tools.name: deeptime
tools.description: Markov state models, TICA/VAMP and kinetic analysis of long or many-replica trajectories.

tools.name: BioSimSpace
tools.description: Interoperable layer for building and running MD and alchemical free-energy workflows across engines.

tools.name: OpenPathSampling
tools.description: Transition path sampling and interface sampling for rare events where you care about the mechanism and rate, not just the endpoints.

tools.name: gamd-openmm
tools.description: The OpenMM implementation of GaMD — the easiest route to accelerated sampling on a GPU without leaving Python.

tools.name: easyPARM
tools.description: Automates force field parameter derivation for metal complexes and organometallics from a QM optimisation, producing ready-to-run Amber, GROMACS, CHARMM and OpenMM inputs.

tools.name: OMMProtocol
tools.description: Runs a complete OpenMM pipeline, from minimisation through equilibration to production, from one YAML file, with checkpointing and standard reporters.

tools.name: AMBER / AmberTools
tools.description: Amber force fields and simulation stack; AmberTools is free, pmemd.CUDA is licensed.

tools.name: CHARMM-GUI
tools.description: Web system builder that sets up membranes, glycans, ligands and solvated systems for every major MD engine.

tools.name: Espaloma
tools.description: Graph-neural-network force-field parameter assignment, replacing atom typing with learned chemistry.

tools.name: FEP+ (Schrödinger)
tools.description: Commercial relative binding free-energy platform, the industry reference for lead-optimisation potency prediction.

tools.name: GaMD
tools.description: Gaussian accelerated MD: adds a harmonic boost potential to flatten energy barriers, reaching microsecond-scale conformational transitions without a predefined reaction coordinate. Implemented in AMBER, NAMD and OpenMM.

tools.name: GPathFinder
tools.description: Finds the route a ligand takes in and out of a buried site by multi-objective search over GaudiMM, giving binding pathways and intermediate poses rather than only the bound state.

tools.name: MACE / MACE-OFF
tools.description: Equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials, including transferable organic force fields for biomolecular systems.

tools.name: MCPB.py
tools.description: AmberTools' metal centre parameter builder: derives bonded-model force field parameters for a metal site from QM, the standard route to simulating a metalloprotein without the ion drifting out.

tools.name: NAMD
tools.description: Scalable MD for very large systems on HPC, paired with VMD for setup and analysis.

tools.name: OpenMM-ML
tools.description: Mixed ML/MM simulation in OpenMM: treat the ligand with a neural potential and the rest classically.

tools.name: ParmEd
tools.description: Reads, edits and converts parameter/topology files between AMBER, CHARMM, GROMACS and OpenMM.

tools.name: SuMD
tools.description: Supervised MD: biases nothing but discards trajectories heading the wrong way, so ligand binding and unbinding pathways emerge in accessible wall-clock time.

tools.name: Psi4
tools.description: Open-source quantum chemistry (DFT, MP2, CC) with a Python API suited to automated workflows.

tools.name: xtb
tools.description: Semiempirical GFNn-xTB methods: geometry, frequencies and energies fast enough for thousands of molecules.

tools.name: NWChem
tools.description: Scalable HPC quantum chemistry for large systems and plane-wave/molecular hybrids.

tools.name: CREST
tools.description: Conformer-rotamer ensemble sampling on top of xtb; the standard cheap conformational search.

tools.name: autodE
tools.description: Automated reaction-profile generation: conformers, transition states and barriers with minimal manual setup.

tools.name: AIMNet2
tools.description: Neural network potential covering neutral, charged and open-shell organic molecules across most of the periodic table — QM-quality energies at force-field cost.

tools.name: ESIgen
tools.description: Turns raw quantum chemistry output into a formatted supporting information document: geometries, energies, frequencies and images, from a template.

tools.name: Garleek
tools.description: Bridges Gaussian's ONIOM to molecular mechanics backends such as Tinker and OpenMM, so a QM/MM job can put a metal centre in the QM layer and the rest of the protein in MM.

tools.name: Multiwfn
tools.description: Wavefunction analysis: bond orders, charges, orbital composition, electron density topology and non-covalent interaction plots from the output of most QM programs.

tools.name: ORCA
tools.description: Broad-capability QM package, free for academic use; common for spectroscopy and mechanism work.

tools.name: PySCF
tools.description: Python-native electronic structure library, easy to embed in ML and screening pipelines.

tools.name: pysisyphus
tools.description: Optimises stationary points on reaction paths: chain-of-states methods, transition state searches and intrinsic reaction coordinates, driving whichever QM engine you have.

tools.name: RDKit
tools.description: The open cheminformatics toolkit everything else is built on: descriptors, fingerprints, conformers, substructure search, reaction handling.

tools.name: Open Babel
tools.description: Chemical file format interconversion, 3D coordinate generation and conformer search across 110+ formats.

tools.name: CDK
tools.description: Chemistry Development Kit: the mature Java cheminformatics library (descriptors, fingerprints, IO).

tools.name: ScaffoldGraph
tools.description: Builds scaffold trees and networks over a library, so you can see which chemotypes a screening set actually covers and where a series sits.

tools.name: CReM
tools.description: Chemically reasonable mutations: fragment-based structure generation with medicinal-chemistry-valid replacements.

tools.name: Mordred
tools.description: 1,800+ 2D/3D molecular descriptors on top of RDKit; the classical descriptor baseline for QSAR.

tools.name: Ketcher
tools.description: Web structure editor for sketching molecules and reactions in browser-based apps.

tools.name: Datamol
tools.description: Ergonomic RDKit wrapper for standardisation, featurisation and parallel molecular processing.

tools.name: Indigo
tools.description: EPAM's cheminformatics toolkit for structure handling, reaction processing and rendering, with bindings for several languages.

tools.name: Architector
tools.description: Generates 3D conformers for metal complexes across the periodic table, including multiple spin states and coordination geometries, as a Python API.

tools.name: SwissBioisostere
tools.description: Which substituent replacements have actually been made and what they did to activity, mined from measured data — bioisosteric replacement grounded in evidence rather than intuition.

tools.name: Auto3D
tools.description: Turns SMILES into low-energy 3D structures with correct stereochemistry and tautomer handling — the unglamorous step that silently ruins docking when skipped.

tools.name: Cambridge Structural Database (CCDC)
tools.description: The small-molecule crystal structure archive, over half of it metal-organic. The empirical reference for coordination geometry, bond lengths and ligand conformation.

tools.name: ChEMBL Structure Pipeline
tools.description: The exact standardisation, parent-extraction and salt-stripping rules ChEMBL applies; the reference for reproducible curation.

tools.name: DataWarrior
tools.description: Free desktop app for chemical data visualisation, SAR analysis, clustering and property prediction.

tools.name: Lilly Medchem Rules
tools.description: Eli Lilly's published rule set for rejecting compounds a medicinal chemist would not take forward — reactive groups, known frequent hitters, unstable motifs. A harder filter than PAINS alone.

tools.name: mmpdb
tools.description: Matched molecular pair database from RDKit: extracts which single transformations have been made across a dataset and what they did to a property. The most directly medicinal-chemistry tool in the open stack.

tools.name: molSimplify
tools.description: Builds, optimises and screens transition-metal complexes from a metal, oxidation state and ligand set; generates sane 3D geometries where general-purpose toolkits guess badly.

tools.name: OPSIN
tools.description: Converts IUPAC chemical names to structures; the standard name-to-structure parser.

tools.name: COCONUT
tools.description: Aggregated open natural products collection with structures and source organisms.

tools.name: ChEMBL
tools.description: Manually curated bioactivity database (~2.4M compounds, 20M+ activities) mapped to targets and assays.

tools.name: Chemical Probes Portal
tools.description: Expert review of which chemical probes are actually fit for target validation, and at what concentration.

tools.name: DrugBank
tools.description: Approved and investigational drugs with targets, pharmacology, interactions and ADMET; free academic tier.

tools.name: BindingDB
tools.description: Measured binding affinities (Kd/Ki/IC50) for protein-small molecule pairs, curated from literature and patents.

tools.name: Chemspace
tools.description: Aggregated supplier space — in-stock screening compounds and make-on-demand building blocks in one search.

tools.name: CMAUP
tools.description: Collective molecular activities of useful plants: plant species mapped to their constituents, those constituents to targets, and targets to pathways and diseases.

tools.name: eMolecules
tools.description: Building-block and screening-compound catalogue with supplier stock and pricing, searchable by substructure.

tools.name: Enamine REAL Space
tools.description: Make-on-demand combinatorial space of 6B+ synthesisable compounds with ~80% synthesis success.

tools.name: FooDB
tools.description: The chemistry of food: constituents of plant and animal foods with structures, concentrations and provenance. Useful when the starting point is a dietary source rather than a screening deck.

tools.name: GtoPdb (Guide to Pharmacology)
tools.description: Expert-curated ligand-target pharmacology: selectivity, affinities and recommended tool compounds.

tools.name: IMPPAT
tools.description: Indian medicinal plants, their phytochemicals and therapeutic uses, with curated structures and drug-likeness already computed.

tools.name: Mcule
tools.description: Purchasable compound database with per-compound availability and a free web tier for small searches.

tools.name: NPASS
tools.description: Natural products with measured activities against defined targets, and the species they came from. The quantitative counterpart to structure-only natural product collections.

tools.name: Papyrus
tools.description: A normalised, standardised bioactivity dataset (60M+ points) assembled for ML-ready QSAR modelling — the cleaned-up ChEMBL you were going to build yourself.

tools.name: PDBbind+
tools.description: Experimental binding affinities paired with their PDB complex structures; the basis of the CASF scoring benchmarks (the old pdbbind.org.cn is retired).

tools.name: Phenol-Explorer
tools.description: Measured polyphenol contents of foods, including what processing and cooking do to them. Specific where general natural product databases are silent.

tools.name: PROTAC-DB
tools.description: Curated database of PROTACs with ternary complex data, linker chemistry and measured degradation — the reference set for degrader design.

tools.name: PubChem
tools.description: The largest open chemical database: compounds, substances, bioassays, patents and literature links.

tools.name: SureChEMBL
tools.description: Chemical structures extracted from patents, updated daily; the standard patent-chemistry search.

tools.name: ZINC22
tools.description: Purchasable and make-on-demand compounds prepared for docking in 3D, at tens of billions of molecules.

tools.name: MOSES
tools.description: Benchmarking platform for molecular generative models with standard splits and distribution metrics.

tools.name: REINVENT4
tools.description: AstraZeneca's production generative design framework: reinforcement learning over a multi-parameter scoring function, with scaffold and linker modes.

tools.name: DiffSBDD
tools.description: Equivariant diffusion generating ligands directly inside a protein pocket.

tools.name: DiffLinker
tools.description: Equivariant diffusion for linker design in fragment linking and PROTAC-style problems.

tools.name: TargetDiff
tools.description: 3D diffusion model for structure-based ligand generation; a common baseline for pocket-conditioned design.

tools.name: Fragmenstein
tools.description: Merges and places fragment hits into a single compound that respects the crystallographic positions they came from — built for fragment-based campaigns and XChem-style data.

tools.name: GuacaMol
tools.description: Goal-directed and distribution-learning benchmarks for de novo design, still the common comparison point.

tools.name: LigandMPNN
tools.description: Sequence design conditioned on ligands, nucleotides and cofactors; the successor to ProteinMPNN for binding sites.

tools.name: Pocket2Mol
tools.description: Equivariant generation of 3D molecules conditioned directly on a binding pocket.

tools.name: SAFE
tools.description: Sequential attachment-based fragment embedding: a SMILES rewrite that makes scaffold-constrained generation natural.

tools.name: SeeSAR
tools.description: Interactive structure-based design: grow, replace and link with estimated affinity and torsion strain updating as you edit. The commercial tool medicinal chemists actually enjoy using.

tools.name: DeepChem
tools.description: Long-running deep learning library for chemistry and biology: featurisers, splitters, model zoo and the MoleculeNet task collection.

tools.name: DGL-LifeSci
tools.description: Ready-made GNN models and datasets for property prediction, reaction prediction and generation.

tools.name: Chemprop
tools.description: Directed message-passing neural networks for molecular property prediction — the open baseline that beats descriptor models on most endpoints with enough data, and the engine under ADMET-AI.

tools.name: Uni-Mol
tools.description: 3D-aware molecular representation model used as a pretrained backbone for property and binding tasks.

tools.name: scikit-mol
tools.description: RDKit featurisation wrapped as scikit-learn transformers, so fingerprints and descriptors live inside a Pipeline and cannot leak across a split.

tools.name: ChemBERTa
tools.description: BERT-style pretraining over SMILES — the accessible baseline for whether a pretrained representation beats fingerprints on your endpoint.

tools.name: CheMeleon
tools.description: Foundation model pretrained to reproduce Mordred descriptors, then fine-tuned through Chemprop with --from-foundation CheMeleon; beats descriptor and GNN baselines on small property datasets.

tools.name: DEL-iver
tools.description: Processes DNA-encoded library selections: building-block and disynthon enrichment, binding models on building-block or full-molecule inputs, and analog picking from make-on-demand space. Early research code from a 2026 preprint. The default split is random, which leaks building blocks between tra…

tools.name: KNIME
tools.description: Visual workflow platform with mature chemistry nodes (RDKit, Schrödinger, Vernalis) for no-code pipelines.

tools.name: Mol-JEPA
tools.description: Boehringer Ingelheim's multimodal joint-embedding model, fusing cellular effects, binding affinity, ADMET and quantum chemistry into one molecular representation. Code is unlicensed; the weights are CC BY-NC 4.0.

tools.name: MolFormer
tools.description: IBM's transformer pretrained on a billion molecules; a strong general-purpose embedding when you have too little labelled data to train from scratch.

tools.name: MolSkill
tools.description: Learns medicinal chemists' implicit preferences from pairwise choices to score compound attractiveness.

tools.name: Optuna
tools.description: Hyperparameter optimisation with pruning; the usual companion to model selection in QSAR pipelines.

tools.name: PyTorch Geometric
tools.description: The standard GNN library for molecular graphs: message passing, pooling, batching over molecules.

tools.name: QSARtuna
tools.description: AstraZeneca's automated QSAR model building: preprocessing, algorithm and hyperparameter search, uncertainty.

tools.name: scikit-learn
tools.description: The classical ML baseline stack (RF, SVM, calibration, CV) that every QSAR study is measured against.

tools.name: XGBoost
tools.description: Gradient boosting that remains highly competitive on descriptor/fingerprint tabular chemistry data.

tools.name: OPERA
tools.description: Free, regulatory-grade QSAR models for physchem and ADMET endpoints with applicability domain and AD-based confidence; used by EPA/NIH.

tools.name: ProTox 3.0
tools.description: Toxicity endpoint prediction (organ toxicity, endpoints, pathways, LD50) with similarity and fragment evidence.

tools.name: SwissADME
tools.description: Fast physicochemical, pharmacokinetic and drug-likeness profiling including the BOILED-Egg permeability model.

tools.name: ADMET-AI
tools.description: Fast Chemprop-RDKit ADMET predictions across the TDC endpoint set, with percentile context against approved drugs.

tools.name: ADMETlab 3.0
tools.description: Web predictor covering 88 ADMET endpoints with uncertainty estimates and batch submission.

tools.name: GastroPlus
tools.description: Commercial PBPK/absorption simulation, standard for formulation and oral bioavailability modelling.

tools.name: Open Systems Pharmacology (PK-Sim/MoBi)
tools.description: Open-source PBPK and QSP modelling suite; the free alternative to commercial PBPK platforms.

tools.name: OpenADMET
tools.description: Open consortium generating new experimental ADMET data on the targets that break programmes, and releasing models trained on it — an answer to ADMET models trained on stale public sets.

tools.name: pkCSM
tools.description: Graph-signature-based ADMET prediction across absorption, distribution, metabolism, excretion and toxicity endpoints.

tools.name: Simcyp (Certara)
tools.description: Commercial PBPK simulator used in regulatory submissions for DDI and special-population predictions.

tools.name: vNN-ADMET
tools.description: Variable-nearest-neighbour ADMET models with explicit applicability domain, including DILI and CYP endpoints.

tools.name: RAscore
tools.description: Predicts whether a retrosynthesis planner would find a route, as a fast synthesisability filter.

tools.name: AiZynthFinder
tools.description: Monte-Carlo tree search retrosynthesis over learned templates, with building-block availability built into the search.

tools.name: AiZynthModels
tools.description: AstraZeneca's repository for training, evaluating and using synthesis prediction models, and the replacement for AiZynthTrain. Train AiZynthFinder's models on your own reaction data so in-house chemistry and stock are reflected in the routes.

tools.name: ASKCOS
tools.description: MIT's open retrosynthesis, forward prediction and condition recommendation platform.

tools.name: Chemformer
tools.description: Sequence-to-sequence transformer for reaction prediction and retrosynthesis, pretrained on SMILES and fine-tuned per task. Now maintained inside AiZynthModels; the standalone repository is archived.

tools.name: DRFP
tools.description: Reaction fingerprints without atom mapping or a neural net; a fast, surprisingly strong featuriser for yield and condition models.

tools.name: IBM RXN for Chemistry
tools.description: Transformer-based forward prediction, retrosynthesis and procedure generation as a free web service.

tools.name: Molecular Transformer
tools.description: Sequence-to-sequence forward reaction prediction: given reactants, predict the product. The model most later reaction work is benchmarked against.

tools.name: Open Reaction Database
tools.description: Open, structured reaction data with a defined schema — the public counterweight to proprietary reaction corpora, and the place to put your own.

tools.name: PaRoutes
tools.description: Benchmark of real multi-step routes with the metrics to score a planner against them — how you tell whether a retrosynthesis model is actually better.

tools.name: PostEra Manifold
tools.description: Route search over purchasable space with prices and lead times, plus synthesis-aware analogue search. Free tier covers occasional use.

tools.name: R-SMILES
tools.description: Root-aligned SMILES: a representation change that sharply improves seq2seq retrosynthesis accuracy by minimising the edit distance between product and reactants.

tools.name: rdchiral
tools.description: Correct chirality handling when applying retrosynthetic reaction templates in RDKit.

tools.name: Reaxys
tools.description: Elsevier's reaction and substance database; the precedent search a chemist checks before trusting any predicted route.

tools.name: Retro*
tools.description: Neural A* search over retrosynthesis trees, optimising the whole route rather than greedily picking each disconnection.

tools.name: RetroChimera
tools.description: Microsoft Research's single-step retrosynthesis model, built by ensembling two components with complementary inductive biases. Learns from very few examples per reaction class, and its predictions were preferred by industrial chemists in blind tests. Built on Syntheseus; installable from PyPI.

tools.name: RetroSim
tools.description: Similarity-based retrosynthesis: find precedent reactions for similar molecules and transfer the disconnection. The baseline every neural planner should beat, and often does not.

tools.name: RXNMapper
tools.description: Atom-maps reactions from an attention-based model with no templates — the preprocessing step that template extraction and most reaction ML quietly depend on.

tools.name: SCScore
tools.description: Synthetic complexity score learned from reaction corpora, complementing the classic SA score.

tools.name: Spaya
tools.description: Iktos' retrosynthesis service scoring routes on feasibility and building-block availability.

tools.name: SYBA
tools.description: Bayesian classifier for synthetic accessibility trained on easy vs hard molecules — a different signal from SAscore, useful as a second opinion.

tools.name: Syntheseus
tools.description: Benchmarking and inference framework that puts retrosynthesis models on a common, fairly evaluated footing.

tools.name: Synthia
tools.description: Merck's expert-rules retrosynthesis platform (formerly Chematica) — hand-encoded chemistry rather than learned templates, and strong on stereochemistry.

tools.name: AbLang2
tools.description: Antibody language model for restoring missing residues and generating germline-plausible sequences.

tools.name: ABodyBuilder3
tools.description: Fast, accurate antibody Fv structure prediction with per-residue confidence on the CDR loops.

tools.name: ANARCI
tools.description: Antibody numbering and germline assignment (IMGT, Kabat, Chothia); the preprocessing step for antibody ML.

tools.name: ESM
tools.description: Evolutionary-scale protein language models (ESM-2, ESMFold), used for embeddings, variant effect scores and as the front end of structure prediction without an MSA. This repository is archived; the newer models in the line (ESM C, ESMFold2, ESM3) are developed at Biohub/esm under their own licence.

tools.name: FireProt
tools.description: Automated design of thermostable variants, combining energy- and evolution-based predictions into a short list of mutations worth making rather than a ranked dump of all of them.

tools.name: FoldX
tools.description: Empirical force field for fast stability and binding ddG on point mutations; free academic licence.

tools.name: IgBLAST
tools.description: NCBI's immunoglobulin/TCR V(D)J assignment tool for repertoire sequencing.

tools.name: ImmuneBuilder
tools.description: Fast antibody, nanobody and TCR structure prediction with accuracy competitive on CDR loops.

tools.name: Observed Antibody Space (OAS)
tools.description: Billions of cleaned, numbered antibody repertoire sequences; the pretraining corpus for antibody models.

tools.name: Protein-Sol
tools.description: Sequence-based prediction of heterologous expression solubility in E. coli, scaled against an experimental set; a cheap first read on whether a construct will express before anyone orders it.

tools.name: ProteinMPNN
tools.description: Inverse folding: given a backbone, designs sequences that fold to it. The workhorse of modern de novo protein design.

tools.name: PyRosetta
tools.description: Python interface to Rosetta for design, docking, loop modelling and energy calculations; free academic licence.

tools.name: RFdiffusion
tools.description: Diffusion-based generation of protein backbones, including binders to a specified target site.

tools.name: RosettaCommons
tools.description: The Rosetta software suite for macromolecular modelling and design, and its licensing/community hub.

tools.name: SAbDab / SAbPred
tools.description: Curated structural antibody database plus the OPIG prediction suite (paratope, epitope, developability, TAP).

tools.name: ThermoMPNN
tools.description: Graph network predicting the change in folding stability for every point mutation in a structure, fast enough to scan a whole protein.

tools.name: ClinicalTrials.gov
tools.description: Registry of 500k+ trials with a modern API; the source for competitive and trial-design landscaping.

tools.name: DailyMed
tools.description: Current FDA structured product labels (SPL), machine-readable and updated daily.

tools.name: Drugs@FDA
tools.description: Approval history, review documents and labels for FDA-approved drugs.

tools.name: EMA Medicines
tools.description: European public assessment reports and product information for centrally authorised medicines.

tools.name: Espacenet
tools.description: The European Patent Office's search over 140 million patent documents, with family and legal-status data that the free aggregators do not carry.

tools.name: Europe PMC
tools.description: Full-text life-science literature with annotations and a solid API for text mining.

tools.name: Google Patents
tools.description: Full-text patent search across the major offices with chemical structure indexing; the practical first look at whether a scaffold is already claimed.

tools.name: openFDA
tools.description: APIs over FDA drug labels, adverse events (FAERS), recalls and device data.

tools.name: PubMed / NCBI E-utilities
tools.description: Biomedical citation index and the E-utilities API behind most literature pipelines.

tools.name: SIDER
tools.description: Side-effect resource linking marketed drugs to label-extracted adverse reactions and frequencies.

tools.name: LIT-PCBA
tools.description: Unbiased virtual screening benchmark built from dose-response PubChem assays, designed to avoid DUD-E's biases.

tools.name: MoleculeACE
tools.description: Activity-cliff benchmark: curated bioactivity data on 30 targets, with the tooling to score how a QSAR model does on near-identical molecules whose potency differs sharply. The test a model's headline accuracy hides. Supports Python 3.8 only, and some deep-learning dependencies are installed sepa…

tools.name: Therapeutics Data Commons
tools.description: 66+ AI-ready therapeutic datasets with fixed splits and leaderboards, spanning ADMET to biologics.

tools.name: PoseCheck
tools.description: Physical-plausibility checks (strain energy, steric clashes, interactions) for structure-based generative models.

tools.name: DUD-E
tools.description: Directory of useful decoys, enhanced: actives with property-matched decoys for virtual-screening evaluation.

tools.name: MoleculeNet
tools.description: The original standard property-prediction benchmark suite (ESOL, FreeSolv, BACE, Tox21, …).

tools.name: Polaris
tools.description: Community platform for rigorous, versioned benchmarks in drug-discovery ML with leak-resistant splits.

tools.name: PoseBusters
tools.description: Checks whether a predicted pose is physically possible at all — geometry, stereochemistry, clashes with the protein. The standard sanity gate for generated poses.

tools.name: 3Dmol.js
tools.description: WebGL structure viewer, and through its py3Dmol binding the quickest way to eyeball docking poses inside a notebook.

tools.name: PyChimera
tools.description: Use the UCSF Chimera Python API from an ordinary interpreter, so Chimera's structure handling can be scripted inside a normal pipeline instead of its own shell.

tools.name: Cytoscape
tools.description: The platform network pharmacology is done on: build a compound-target-pathway network, lay it out, score the hubs, and see what the topology actually says.

tools.name: Mol*
tools.description: The web molecular viewer used by RCSB and PDBe; embeddable in any internal tool.

tools.name: NGL Viewer
tools.description: Lightweight WebGL structure viewer, and the nglview Jupyter widget built on it.

tools.name: PyMOL (open source)
tools.description: The de facto structure viewer for figures and pose inspection; open-source build plus a commercial edition.

tools.name: Tangram
tools.description: A suite of UCSF Chimera extensions from the same group: QM and QM/MM setup, PLIP interaction depiction, PropKa states, normal modes, and dummy-atom preparation of metal systems for MD. Free for academic use.

tools.name: UCSF ChimeraX
tools.description: Modern successor to Chimera: large structures, cryo-EM maps, AlphaFold integration and scripting.

tools.name: VMD
tools.description: Trajectory visualisation and analysis for MD, with scripting and rendering for publication figures.

tools.name: Dask
tools.description: Parallel dataframes and task graphs for larger-than-memory chemical datasets.

tools.name: DVC
tools.description: Git-style versioning for datasets and model artefacts, so screening data stays reproducible.

tools.name: Hugging Face Hub
tools.description: Where most released protein and molecule model weights and datasets now live.

tools.name: MLflow
tools.description: Experiment tracking, model registry and packaging; the usual answer to 'which model made this prediction'.

tools.name: Nextflow
tools.description: Dataflow workflow engine with containerised, resumable execution across HPC and cloud; nf-core supplies vetted pipelines.

tools.name: PyTorch Lightning
tools.description: Training-loop framework that standardises multi-GPU training and checkpointing for molecular models.

tools.name: Ray
tools.description: Distributed execution for parallel docking, simulation sweeps and model training on one API.

tools.name: Snakemake
tools.description: Python-based workflow manager with conda/container integration, common for bioinformatics pipelines.
